small_guidance:
- The atomic_add across spatial tiles is the main bottleneck — increase BLOCK_SP to cover the full OW row (or larger) so fewer programs contribute per (N, OC), and consider eliminating the atomic by accumulating the full spatial reduction within a single program (grid over (N, OC tile) only, loop over spatial internally).
- Autotune over (BLOCK_OC ∈ {32,64,128}, BLOCK_SP ∈ {128,256,512}, num_warps ∈ {4,8}, num_stages ∈ {2,3}) — current 64/256/8w may be under-utilizing registers given the small IC=8.
- Cache the weight tile once outside the spatial loop (load all OC×K weights into registers per program) since K = 8*3*3 = 72 is tiny — then the spatial loop only streams inputs.
large_guidance:
- Redesign as one program per (N, OC tile) that loads the entire weight slice (OC_tile × IC×KH×KW) into registers up front, then streams over output spatial positions in chunks accumulating a scalar partial-sum per OC channel — output is just (N, OC), so the reduction lives entirely in-register and writes once with no atomics.
- Use a channels-last (NHWC) input layout so the IC dimension is contiguous; this lets the inner kh/kw loop do a single vectorized load across IC and turn the conv into a small dot-product per spatial point.
- Alternatively, since OH*OW ≈ 254² is large and OC*N = 8192 is modest, persistent-program over spatial tiles with cross-block reduction via tl.sum on a (BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_SP) tile and a single store per (N, OC tile) — drop atomic_add entirely.
